ops.title: proc spawn gate: busy-spin on coordination-pipe EOF + TERM-immunity orphans workers
ops.description:
Found via 43h-wedged daemonkit-worker (PID 4829, yasyf box, 2026-07-25) with sample+lsof forensics; control case PID 40403 (identical preamble, healthy blocking read) isolates the defect. The spawn shell preamble runs:

  trap ':' TERM
  printf r >&3
  exec 3>&-
  while ! IFS= read -r _ <&4; do :; done
  exec 4<&-
  trap - TERM
  exec "$@" <&5

When the coordination pipe's (fd 4) write end vanishes — spawner/harness died mid-gate — `read` returns EOF, which is a shell failure, so `! read` is true and the loop busy-spins at ~100% CPU forever instead of blocking. Worse, `trap ':' TERM` is armed for the whole gate, so the wedged worker ignores SIGTERM — the normal kill/reap path cannot collect it; only SIGKILL works. Observed: 43.2h CPU, PPID 1, pure interpreter spin (sample: strcmp under repeating eval frames, zero syscall blocking).

Fix shape: distinguish EOF from EINTR in the gate — e.g. exit (or proceed to cleanup) on EOF instead of retrying, and/or bound the TERM-trap window.

Evidence artifacts: /tmp/wedged-4829-sample.txt + /tmp/wedged-4829-lsof.txt (yasyf box), mirrored in the sweep transcript. Surfaced by claude-pool's TestPrepareAccountBackingDeadlineKillsReapsAndUntracks leftover — the exact kill/reap path that test claims to prove is the one TERM-immunity defeats.

Sequencing: NOT in the frozen baseline (4497f65 release) — land via normal flow after fleet convergence per the release freeze.

ops.text: killing the spawner mid-gate leaves no spinning worker (worker exits on pipe EOF)
a gate-phase worker responds to TERM or is reaped by Recover
